The Two Preimages of a Folded Point

Source: R/folded.R
fold_parts.Rd

Computes the parent's density at \(+x\) and at \(-x\), their sum, and the weight \(w = f(x)/L(x)\) of the positive preimage. Every method of FoldedDistrib needs the same four quantities, so they are formed once per call: the density is \(L\), the score is \(w s(x) + (1-w) s(-x)\), and every higher-order ratio is a \(w\)-weighted average of the parent's own.

Usage

fold_parts(parent, x, theta)

Arguments

parent

The wrapped continuous_distrib object.

x

A numeric vector of points at which to evaluate. Negative values are not screened out here; the calling method zeroes them.

theta

A named list of the parent's parameters.

Value

A named list of four numeric vectors of the recycled length: fp and fm, the parent's density at \(+x\) and \(-x\); L, their sum; and w, the ratio fp / L.

Details

At \(x = 0\) the two preimages coincide, so \(w = 1/2\) whatever the parameters are and the folded density is exactly twice the parent's. Far out in the tail of a parent centered above zero, \(w\) approaches one and the fold becomes invisible.

Notation

\(f\) is the parent's density, \(L\) the folded one, \(w\) the weight of the positive preimage and \(s\) the parent's score.

See also

fold_ratio() for the higher-order quantities built on these, and distrib_pdf.FoldedDistrib() for the first consumer.

Examples

g <- gaussian1_distrib()
theta <- list(mu = 0.5, sigma = 1.2)
p <- distributions7:::fold_parts(g, c(0, 1, 3), theta)
str(p)
#> List of 4
#>  $ fp: num [1:3] 0.305 0.305 0.038
#>  $ fm: num [1:3] 0.30481 0.15221 0.00473
#>  $ L : num [1:3] 0.6096 0.457 0.0427
#>  $ w : num [1:3] 0.5 0.667 0.889

# L is the sum of the two preimages, which is the folded density.
all.equal(p$L, dnorm(c(0, 1, 3), 0.5, 1.2) + dnorm(-c(0, 1, 3), 0.5, 1.2))
#> [1] TRUE

# At zero the two preimages coincide, so the weight is exactly one half.
p$w[1]
#> [1] 0.5

# And far into the tail the fold becomes invisible: w approaches one.
distributions7:::fold_parts(g, c(3, 6, 12), theta)$w
#> [1] 0.8892727 0.9847328 0.9997597
